observations.B01: Two entire lines are crossed by long horizontal strokes. Ascenders support structure and pondérés; the final word of line one and the first short word of line two remain uncertain under the cancellation. The tiny ink tip at the lower crop edge belongs to the next line and is excluded.
observations.B02: The upper replacement has a descending initial p, a tall middle t, and terminal els, read ponctuels. Below it the struck initial à retains an isolated accent; the next word has a long descender and a dotted stroke toward its end, but the strike conceals the connecting letters. Closing parenthesis retained.
observations.B03: Fresh crop rotated 90 degrees clockwise. Small interlinear i.e. codim. modulaire nulle has a long insertion guide returning to the parenthesis after isolé. Main-line numeral read 1. A separate lower cancelled word is physically obscured; the following relation sign is uncertain, and its final 1 is visible. Heavy terminal border or cancellation stroke has no recoverable lettering.
observations.B04: Equation number reads 70. Upper dot has 4 above and g=0 below; lower dot has 1 above and g=1 below. Both Gamma superscripts have a separate point beneath the vertical stroke, so they are exclamation marks. Upper group symbol is an elaborate looped capital with clear subscript 4; fraktur S is uncertain. Both point drawings and the grouping brace are retained in TikZ.
observations.B05: MD- is above the baseline and attached by a curved insertion mark before graphes. The incomplete preceding word at the left edge is excluded.
observations.B06: Initial r, tall t, separated low middle strokes, and looped l support rationnels. Opening and closing quotation marks are visible, with one underline beneath the word.
observations.B07: The word after sommets has an apostrophe and the low sequence ordre. The formula has a wavy tilde, a descending mu, subscript alpha, and two less-than-or-equal signs. A small top-edge fragment from the previous line is excluded.
observations.B08: A horizontal strike crosses the lower et que; the upper replacement reads sauf l’. The long lower descender belongs to que and is not a separate mathematical mark.
observations.B09: The first line ends égal à 4 (donc. The following mu has a wavy upper mark and a small zero after subscript alpha. MD- is interlinear with a curved insertion guide before graphes. No formula hat is substituted for the wavy mark.
observations.B10: The initial short word is heavily overwritten at its first character; ont is tentative. The subsequent tous leurs sommets is legible from the tall t and looped l.
observations.B11: Hat over nu in the first formula is angular; the later nu at far right has no upper decoration. The cancelled word after the comma is uncertain because the horizontal strike covers its low letters. Alpha-zero is written above the gap after un with an insertion stroke. In the parenthesis the mu subscript shows alpha but no distinct following zero. Top-left edge ink belongs to the preceding line and is excluded.
observations.B12: The wavy mark above mu is a tilde; nu later in the line is undecorated. Pour alpha not-equal alpha-zero is above the line and attached before sont with a long guide. The minor ink at the upper left is from the preceding line and is excluded.
observations.B13: The cancelled words show pour followed by alpha and a not-equal sign; no further subscript or operand is visible in that struck phrase. The final zero is heavily filled but oval. Lower-edge ink from the following line and the neighboring parenthetical insertion is excluded here.
observations.B14: The first g has a clearly separated alpha and small zero below. The second subscript is tightly joined and may be alpha-zero or alpha; both readings are retained. A curved guide enters from the lower left, so the parenthesis is treated as inserted. Lower-edge fragments of the following line are excluded.
observations.B15: The left word is two low connected humps, read un. The next abbreviation has a dotted i followed by s and a closed o. The small bottom-edge apex belongs to the formula below and is excluded.
observations.B16: Number 71 and both M hats are clear. The subscript under the first M is a looped G rather than the angular Gamma written in B04. The relation is a wavy stroke over one horizontal line. The I in the right subscript has an angular hat. Cropped words along the upper edge belong to the preceding prose line and are excluded.
observations.B17: The note begins avec. I has an angular hat while A has a wavy tilde. Cardinal is followed by 4 ou 1 and a comma; the descending comma lies above the second g on the next line and is not a g accent. The final parenthesis reaches the right edge. A top-edge descender from the preceding prose is excluded.
observations.B18: Pencil foliation reads 56; the second digit has an enclosed lower loop. It is kept as margin writing rather than an authorial page-number command.
observations.B19: The tall t after the initial ra, dotted i, low double-n sequence, and final looped l support rationnels. No underline or quotation marks appear in this box. A small top-edge descender from the preceding line is excluded.
